note: House terminology for machine translation and for auditing existing message/blog files.
`avoid` lists variants that lose to the house term, so `check` can flag them.
Provenance differs by term. The 22 terms through 'Antwerp' are uniglo-diamonds-web's
own house terms, taken from ITS shipped, human-translated messages/<locale>.json —
real dominant usage, not invented.
The 6 terms from 'bezel' onward are Aurelia-specific additions. Aurelia's own
messages/*.json cannot serve as evidence for them: every locale file is still entirely
English (translation has not run yet), so there is no shipped Aurelia copy to count.
Instead each was checked against uniglo's shipped corpus (same jewellery domain, real
human translations) by searching for the candidate AND plausible alternatives and
reading the surrounding sentence — raw substring counts alone are misleading (e.g. a
false-friend word can outnumber the real one). Where that corpus gave a clear,
contextually-confirmed jewellery-sense rendering, it was used, with the occurrence count
recorded in the task-11 report's "Fix round 1" section. 'tennis bracelet' is the one
exception seeded alongside them: it duplicated an already-seeded uniglo term, so instead
of a second conflicting entry, the uniglo value was kept (and, after a round-1 review
fix, actually restored — an earlier draft of this file briefly had the wrong, invented
Spanish value here; see the report).
Terms not found in the reference corpus; to be confirmed by a native speaker:
- 'bail' (all five): uniglo's shipped corpus contains the concept ZERO times — no
English 'bail'/'bale', and none of 'anilla'/'asa'/'argolla' (es), 'bélière' (fr),
'anellino'/'contromaglia' (it), 'Öse' (de) or 'hangoog' (nl) appears anywhere in its
140 JSON files. So unlike every term above, this row CANNOT cite the reference
corpus. It records instead the dominant rendering already in Aurelia's own 107
English 'bail' leaves (es anilla 41 occ / asa 30 / argolla 26; fr bélière 103;
it anellino 30 / contromaglia 12; de Öse 56 / Anhängeröse 30; nl hangoog 47 /
hangeroog 23) — machine output, so evidence of consistency, not of correctness.
The `avoid` list is deliberately limited to 'reasa', which is not a Spanish word at
all (a hallucination this row exists to prevent recurring). The real-word variants
'asa' and 'argolla' are NOT banned: they are defensible Spanish, banning them would
make `check` report ~50 violations nobody has reviewed, and a bad glossary row gets
ENFORCED by `check` rather than caught. Marked `unvalidated` for all five.
- 'station necklace' (es): the ONLY 'station chain' sentence in uniglo's entire
corpus was translated into Spanish by avoiding the concept entirely ('cadena de
diamantes espaciada' — no 'station' word at all). fr/it/de/nl values for this term
rest on that same single parallel sentence (N=1) — real translator output, but thin
evidence, not a dominant pattern. Marked via `unvalidated` below.
To research a new entry: node scripts/i18n/translate.mjs terms "<english term>"
